speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we hope this will fuel our students’ intrinsic motivation to learn, and help them discover their interests and passions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond HBL and Blended Learning, our teachers are also transforming the in-class learning experience, to be more inquiry-based and experiential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last week, I visited Lakeside Primary School, which is piloting the use of immersive technology to enhance learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I joined a Primary 5 class for their Science lesson on the human respiratory system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Very relevant in the pandemic, as all of us know.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We put on virtual reality (VR) goggles, we examined a pair of lungs up close in a VR environment and learned about how the lungs function.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was wonderful to see how engaged the students were – they were enjoying themselves, they were curious, and asking many questions and excited about learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is just one example of the kind of holistic teaching and learning that our schools are engaged in today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will continue to find new ways to ignite our students’ curiosity and support their development into self-directed and passionate life-long learners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides schools, the Institutes of Higher Learning, the IHLs, are also looking at more holistic education outcomes, something which Mr Darryl David spoke passionately about.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are fundamentally re-thinking existing structures and methods to better meet today’s demands and they are also sharpening their focus on the inculcation of life skills that are important across all disciplines.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, IHLs are putting greater emphasis on experiential learning through projects outside the classroom.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such applied and hands-on experiences help to impart valuable skills like teamwork and negotiation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Often, industry partners are brought on board, giving our students valuable exposure in tackling real-world issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another important change is the expansion of interdisciplinary learning in our IHLs’ curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This builds on the broad-based education provided in our schools, where our students are exposed to a wide range of subjects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that some of the best thinking happens when different fields, ideas and disciplines intersect.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why it is important to expose students to different ways of thinking; to develop hybrid skills, as Ms Phua highlighted just now.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is similar to how an athlete does cross-training to exercise different key muscle groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, interdisciplinary learning is something that is happening across our IHLs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These systematic changes are being made at the Autonomous Universities (AUs) and Polytechnics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, the Universities are enhancing the common curricula for their undergraduates, to equip them with core skills and multidisciplinary knowledge; and give students more room to pursue electives that they enjoy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As students start specialising in particular disciplines, they will also be given greater flexibility to pursue double degrees, double majors, minors and electives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, similar shifts are being made in the Polytechnics, where students will be exposed to a greater breadth of learning and modules.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When it comes to teaching and learning outcomes, our educators are at the forefront of all our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They, too, believe strongly in developing students holistically, and in nurturing key values and competencies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, MOE will do more to support our teachers in this important work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This centre will work with schools to strengthen CCE learning, conduct relevant research, and provide thought leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our goal is for every teacher to be a CCE teacher and we will provide them full support to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We now have one such Centre at Yusof Ishak Secondary School.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It allows teachers to train in situ, strengthening the nexus between research, theory and practice.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Teachers are able to participate in master classes and demonstration classes, apply their learning in an authentic classroom setting, and explore innovative ideas in curriculum and pedagogy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE shares his desire for a more effective performance management system, and we will refine and calibrate how to do this better over time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to use our regular dialogue sessions with the Public Service Division and the teachers’ unions, to ensure that our appraisal framework is relevant, fair and motivates performance and development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also look out for the well-being of teachers in specialised subjects like Arts, Music, PE and Mother Tongue, something which Mr Patrick Tay highlighted earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to run comprehensive staff engagement surveys, something which we are already doing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will engage all our teachers and support them holistically in their professional development as well as their career progression.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our second priority area is to provide more diverse and flexible pathways for learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Whenever I visit our schools and tertiary institutions, I see an incredible diversity of talents and passions amongst our youths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every student is unique, and we must do our utmost to empower each of them to learn, grow and thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are pressing on with major structural changes in our education system, to provide more flexibility for our students to customise their learning experiences, and embrace a wider spectrum of strengths and talents through diverse pathways and through every phase of their learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will support a shift away from an over-emphasis on academic results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because with wider scoring bands, there is no need to chase every last mark.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every student will be measured on their own progress and can set their own goals, regardless of how their peers performed.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More schools will also have the same cut-off point.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we encourage parents and students to look beyond cut-off points and pick a school based on its programmes, its ethos and culture, and that best fits the student’s interests and aptitudes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng and Mr Gerald Giam spoke about this and, indeed, MOE has been progressively preparing students and engaging parents for these changes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, our teachers will continue to advise parents and students on the subject combination that best caters to the student’s pace of learning, based on their learning outcomes, aptitude and attitude.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, if a student who initially takes a subject at the Foundation level shows improvement, then the school will support them to take the subject at the Standard-level for PSLE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Students who do well in their Foundation subject at PSLE or later can also take subjects at a more demanding level in Secondary school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE will continue to put out more information and engage parents on these PSLE changes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But each time we put out this information, I think parents will look at all the details very carefully and I want to remind everyone that the PSLE is just one checkpoint of many in the education journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I think Mr Darryl David just now said it is the "mother of all examinations".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In these schools, students of different academic abilities are placed in mixed form classes, and they can offer additional subjects at a more demanding level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the initial findings from these pilot schools are very encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Students in the mixed form classes are learning well and they are making friends with classmates from different courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More importantly, they are learning to respect and appreciate each other’s differences and strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And with a greater diversity of perspectives, classroom discussions are richer and livelier.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some students attempting subjects at a more demanding level were naturally apprehensive at the start.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But with support and encouragement from their teachers and classmates, they have been progressing well in their learning and enjoying their lessons.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The implementation of Full SBB is not a trivial exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Significant adjustments are needed: our schools in the arrangement of classes and timetables; our teachers in how they design and teach classes for varying student profiles; and our students in their mindsets and attitudes towards learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I am glad that everyone has risen to the challenge and embraced these changes and we are on track to implementing Full SBB across the system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to learn from the experiences of the pilot schools, and more schools will come on board the Full SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will then see the end of streaming and a new approach across all our Secondary schools – giving students greater agency in their own education, and more opportunities to develop their diverse strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also expanding and enhancing our post-Secondary pathways to better support students with different abilities and talents and to ensure that they have more opportunities to progress to post-Secondary courses that are in line with their interests and strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, we will take steps to enhance our Polytechnic and ITE education, to ensure that it remains responsive to the aspirations of our students and the needs of our future economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second Minister Maliki Osman is leading a comprehensive review of opportunities and pathways in applied education, and will share more about this later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the Polytechnics, we are looking to expand the Common Entry Programmes (CEPs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through the CEP, students benefit from exposure to different course options within the cluster as well as career guidance support.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It allows them to discover their interests and strengths, and better understand the nature of each course, before they decide on a specific diploma course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, ITE offers two-year Nitec programmes, and Higher Nitec programmes most of which are two years in duration.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to do more to help these students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are reviewing the ITE curriculum structure to see how to enable more ITE students to attain and benefit from a Higher Nitec certification.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many ITE students want to pursue a diploma, and we will help them do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some do well at ITE and they go on to the Polytechnics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: ITE itself offers Technical diplomas and Work Study diplomas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are different from the Polytechnic diplomas as they put greater emphasis on technical and applied learning, and they integrate work experience into the education journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will expand these distinctive diploma offerings in ITE, so that more students can benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har spoke about quality Private Education Institutions and how they can complement our public system and fill talent gaps in specialised fields like the arts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, MOE believes strongly in the need to nurture more diverse talents through our multiple education pathways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In our next phase of development, we will need this diversity of talent – in STEM and also in the arts, design and media.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, therefore, take steps to strengthen arts education in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE) and the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) are our home-grown private arts education institutions, supported by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They offer specialised arts and design diplomas as well as degree programmes in partnership with overseas universities, like Goldsmiths, the Royal College of Music, and the University of the Arts London.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The programmes are subsidised by MOE, enabling students to access a quality and affordable arts education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have attracted high-quality faculty, many of whom have contributed significantly to the wider cultural sector in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their graduates have also forged diverse and successful careers and contributed to our society and the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have discussed with the boards and management teams in both institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that LASALLE and NAFA have grown from strength to strength over the years to become centres of artistic excellence, with their own unique character and strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, both institutions recognise the opportunity to come together and forge closer collaboration, and to leverage their respective strengths and traditions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, MOE, with MCCY's support, will work with LASALLE and NAFA to establish an alliance between the two institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will be a private University, supported by the Government, with LASALLE and NAFA as its two constituent colleges.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, both will remain as distinct colleges offering their own programmes, and the University will draw on strengths from both colleges and drive synergies between them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, students in future can benefit from a more diverse range of offerings, with more opportunities to access cross-institution modules and projects, as well as share learning resources.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Faculty can look forward to more opportunities for joint academic collaborations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More importantly, we envisage the University to contribute more to cultural life in Singapore and the region, and to offer a stronger value proposition to its students and stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have provided a broad sketch of what this alliance will look like in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a lot of work to be done in putting this together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope the new Arts University will take tertiary arts education in Singapore to greater heights, enabling our youths with strengths and talents in this field to maximise their potential and contribute to our economy and our society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our efforts to expand pathways and opportunities are not limited to the schooling years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the past, most of us saw education and the workplace as two separate worlds.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have a fixed period of education, frontloaded when we are young, followed by a fixed period of work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this model is no longer relevant today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We need a rotational model, where work and education are rotated through one's career, and there are multiple entry points for education through life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is an important shift we are making across our entire system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have to look at the University Cohort Participation Rate, or the CPR, in this broader context.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the CPR for fresh school-leavers is just one pathway to University.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also expanded opportunities for working adults to pursue a degree, for example, through part-time degree programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, those who wish to enter the workforce first can get a clearer sense of their interests and areas they want to deepen their skills in, and then make more informed choices about upgrading later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pandemic has also thrown into sharp relief how essential reskilling and upskilling are for our workers today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is why MOE has enhanced our support for Singaporeans and companies to pursue workplace training during this period.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The various schemes have helped our fresh graduates from University, Polytechnics and ITE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has cushioned the impact of the pandemic and allowed us to avoid the high unemployment rates seen in many other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also paying close attention to mid-career workers whose jobs are impacted and who need help through work transitions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Patrick Tay suggested that we allow PMEs with a local degree to reskill with a second subsidised degree.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I agree fully with Mr Patrick Tay that the IHLs are our key partners in this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They serve not just as a bridge that students cross to enter the workforce, but also a companion for all Singaporeans in their journey of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Overall, MOE is committed to further strengthening this culture of lifelong learning – not just for work reasons, but as a habit and as a way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister of State Gan Siow Huang will say more about this later in her speech.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Reducing inequality and strengthening social mobility has always been our priority, even before COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have made significant moves over the years to ensure that education continues to be an effective social leveller in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have invested in quality and affordable pre-school education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have ensured that those without a conducive home environment can benefit from school-based Student Care Centres and after-school engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are working more closely with community partners to strengthen wrap-around support for disadvantaged students and their families; and we are also providing more support for children with special needs, both in our mainstream schools and in dedicated special education schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second Minister Maliki Osman and Minister of State Sun Xueling will share more on these as well in their speeches.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This commitment to uplift every child is also reflected in our approach to resourcing schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Patrick Tay, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Ms Hazel Poa spoke about class sizes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Poa, in particular, highlighted that there had been a sharp reduction in the teaching force.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I believe she is referring to figures from the Budget Book, and I should clarify that there had been some definitional changes in the Budget Book figures over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, these may not provide a meaningful year-to-year comparison.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, a better source of information to look at the size of our teaching force that is deployed in schools is the Education Statistics Digest which we publish and is made available online.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you look at the data, it will show that while there has been a slight decline in recent years, we have broadly maintained the size of our teaching force.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At its peak, it was about 33,000 or slightly over 33,000 a few years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, just a slight decline, not the sharp fall that Ms Poa highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Also, it is more relevant to compare our teacher numbers with our student enrolment numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, you have got to look at the teaching force in context, compared with student enrolment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When we compute the Pupil-Teacher-Ratio (PTR) in our school system, we find a very clear trend.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is comparable to the OECD averages.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the question is really about how we choose to allocate our teachers across our education system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we are deliberate in deploying them where they can maximise their impact, as part of our needs-based resourcing approach.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we deploy more teachers for students at the earliest grade levels or for those with greater needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Classes are also generally smaller for Secondary students in the Normal (Technical) course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Compared to other OECD countries, we also devote a larger share of our teachers' time to important activities that are crucial for students' holistic development, like CCAs, professional development and lesson preparation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, when Members cite our larger class sizes compared to OECD norms, I hope they understand that it is not that we have fewer teachers, compared to other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also suggested that it is our heavy reliance on private tuition that plays a part in our students doing well in international benchmarks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But really, that is not being very fair to our teachers who work so hard and give so much of themselves for every child in school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, the OECD and other research point to teacher quality as being the critical element in influencing student learning and performance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The bottom line is this – MOE will continue to secure as much resources as we can for the Ministry and we will deploy our teachers in a way that achieves the best outcomes for every child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Whatever resources we have, MOE will have to prioritise them to achieve our desired outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Hazel Poa asked for more support for those who are outside the mainstream system, including home-schoolers and those in private schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to look into these suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I hope everyone understands that resources are always going to be constrained, and we will need to prioritise them for students in our national system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, beyond support for specific needs through more teachers, these schools are also provided with extra general resourcing – including Student Welfare Officers and Allied Educators.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The schools then have the flexibility to identify, monitor and extend support to such students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This goes beyond just academic support; it includes mentoring, motivational and even holiday programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She had little motivation to attend school, often playing truant, or turning up late for school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She struggled academically and had difficulties getting along with her classmates.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Teachers recognised that her behaviour stemmed from broader issues – low self-esteem, her strained relationship with her parents, and her family's financial difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, her school enrolled her in a mentoring programme, where a volunteer mentor helped her to better understand the challenges she faced and how to overcome them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She participated in group bonding sessions with her peers to strengthen her communication and life skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Her teachers provided her extra support for her schoolwork; while the school counsellor organised counselling sessions for her and her mother.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Her family also received financial support from the school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, things are looking up for this student.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She is motivated and engaged in school, participating actively in class and her CCA.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Her grades have picked up, and her relationships with her parents and classmates have improved.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One important aspect of a rich and meaningful school experience is the CCAs and activities outside the classroom.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: CCAs provide opportunities to develop character, resilience, team spirit and leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are important platforms where students from different schools, different backgrounds and races can interact with one another and form lifelong friendships.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is important we give all our students such exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how appreciation and respect for diversity is imbued at a young age.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I have asked the MOE team to study how we can better support our schools in this area, and ensure that students across all our schools can have a full CCA experience based on their passion and interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The importance of keeping our schools open to students from all backgrounds is also reflected in our Primary 1 registration framework.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this framework, we give priority to some groups like children of school alumni because we want families to build connections to their schools, and for each school to develop its own tradition, history and identity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has helped to give every Singaporean child a chance to enter a Primary school of their choice.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In recent years, we have seen competition for spaces in more popular schools intensify, and more schools having to ballot to allocate places.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such popular schools are not limited to any particular locality.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some people have a perception, only certain area have such popular schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such popular schools are found across all our towns in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am sure Members have received such appeals before.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Wherever our children go for their studies, they will be well served, and well supported to reach their fullest potential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chairman, may I say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: (In Mandarin):    COVID-19 has brought us many new challenges, and also reinforced the importance of 21st Century Competencies such as creative thinking and resilience, which are needed to thrive in future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Knowledge may be finite, butthe world is fast changing and unpredictable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hence, other than knowledge, we should develop in our students a broader set of skills including adaptability and a love for lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also vital that we shape strong values and character, which are the bedrock of every child's success.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will interweave CCE more deliberately throughout our students' entire school experience to teach them to be cyber-savvy, mentally strong, and to appreciate different perspectives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Bilingualism will also continue to be integral to our education system and national identity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A strong foundation in our mother tongues will enable our students to better appreciate their heritage and values and take on opportunities in a rising Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to transform and reimagine education to ensure that our students are future-ready.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But MOE will not be able to do this alone.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our communities and families also have a part to play to lay down the foundations for our children to develop.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We look forward to continuing our partnership in education with our many stakeholders, to bring out the best in every child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pandemic poses huge challenges for countries everywhere.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is also an opportunity to transform and re-imagine education, and to start realising a vision for the future of learning where our children learn with joy, rigour and purpose in schools and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE is seizing this window of opportunity to equip our students with a broader range of competencies; to develop more diverse and flexible pathways of learning through life; and to uplift every child, regardless of their starting point.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will stay open to new ideas and we will continue to engage in careful and thoughtful experimentation to keep our education system ready for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We work with many stakeholders, including our educators, parents and the community at large.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, all of us have a role to play to encourage our children to pursue their passions and interests, instead of focusing only on their academic results; and to be open to the different pathways our children can take throughout life, empowering them to find one that best suits them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We all have a shared interest in bringing out the best in our children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I look forward to continuing and strengthening our partnership in education, to nurture our next generation, and shape the future of our nation together.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, MOE is committed to bring out the best in every student, regardless of their starting point in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce, or UPLIFT, was set up in 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through UPLIFT, we aim to safeguard social mobility and strengthen support for students from disadvantaged families, by helping them to achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Like Mr Eric Chua, many of us have come across these students in our work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They face challenges like irregular attendance, and some struggle with self-confidence and motivation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Oftentimes, we find that they lack a structured home environment after school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While the number of students facing these challenges is small, MOE is committed to ensure that all students have the support that they need to do their best and to grow up well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The school-based SCCs provide a safe and nurturing environment for students after school hours, where they can enjoy lunch, an afternoon snack, complete their homework and participate in various enrichment activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Schools prioritise their students from disadvantaged backgrounds when allocating SCC places, and are committed to expanding capacity where necessary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are concerned about students who may benefit from the SCCs but are not currently enrolled.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thus, all Primary schools have started proactively reaching out to parents of these students this year, to encourage them to enrol their children in these SCCs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The teachers guided families through the enrolment process and streamlined the process for financial support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Secondary schools have put in place the GEAR-UP programme, targeting students who would benefit from more structured after-school supervision and support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These help schools identify students' needs early, to better strengthen and customise their learning and socio-emotional support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond our schools, UPLIFT seeks to provide the necessary support for disadvantaged students and their families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was why we started the UPLIFT Community Pilot in Boon Lay, Kreta Ayer and Woodlands starting January 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In these three towns, we introduced an UPLIFT Town-Level Coordinator, or TLC, to smoothen the flow of information and coordinate support for the family from community agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The work of the TLCs is important, as community agencies might not always be able to identify the children and families who need their support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Conversely, schools might not be aware of all the community resources available to support their students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also recruiting volunteers as UPLIFT family befrienders to check in with the families regularly, mentor and guide them, and assist the TLCs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I recently visited Mohammed Nazri and his wife Mariana, both in their mid-30s.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have five children in Primary school and a sixth child who is just under one year old.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nazri’s TLC has been supporting the family since early 2020 when the children's school attendance was irregular.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The TLC first found out that Nazri and his children lived in Malaysia for several years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When the family returned to Singapore, the children found it difficult to adjust as they were behind their peers academically.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of the first things that the TLC did was to enrol the children in MENDAKI's weekend tuition classes and also work with MENDAKI to source for volunteer academic coaches to mentor and inspire the children and provide more individualised support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As mentioned, UPLIFT's support goes beyond the children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The TLC has been supporting the parents, too.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, he linked up Mariana with AMP Singapore, which has schemes to support her interest in setting up a micro business, to enable her to earn an income while caring for her infant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When the child is ready to be placed in a childcare centre, we will assist her to do so and help her look for a more permanent job.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The TLC will also explore upgrading support for Nazri, who is a food delivery rider, to help him secure a more sustainable job.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Apart from the TLC, the family has been matched with two befrienders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of them is an IT professional, Raj, who has helped the children ease into online learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hear that the children's attendance has improved over the past one year and they are more engaged in their learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I wish Nazri and his family all the very best.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, their story is a powerful reminder of what we can achieve through UPLIFT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, at first glance, we see a vulnerable young family with six very young children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When I met them and saw the smile in their children's faces and eyes light up, I see hope and dreams.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must do all we can to fulfil these hopes and dreams for these children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am confident that, together, we can secure a brighter future for Nazri and his family and many other families like theirs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Community partnerships are key to the success of UPLIFT, and must continue.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many community partners have stepped forward to support students from disadvantaged families, who were disproportionately impacted by the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to bring on board more community partners, work with them to curate suitable programmes and connect them with schools whose students would benefit most.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our work in UPLIFT is a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to press on, working hand-in-hand with the community to ensure no child is left behind.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When I took over as Chairperson of UPLIFT, I wanted to deepen our collaboration with Self-Help Groups and also brought People's Association on board the taskforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have brought valuable expertise and experience to take UPLIFT forward.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also continue to work closely with MSF and other Government agencies to synergise across different initiatives, like ComLink, KidSTART and community programmes like M3.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is part of the Government's commitment to strengthen our social service delivery.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: My team comprises representatives from the public, private and people sectors, many of whom have deep engagements and experience in the ITE and Polytechnic sector, as well as Polytechnic and ITE leaders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past couple of months, we have spoken to over 400 stakeholders, including students and graduates of the Polytechnics and ITE, their parents, employers and industry partners and the staff.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Their perspectives have been valuable in shaping the review's early work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We plan to reach out to more stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Eric Chua reminded us of the important role deep technical skills have in our workforce and society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many shared their aspirations to upgrade themselves, building on the foundation they had acquired in Polytechnic or ITE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All of them wanted to hone their skills to stay up to date in a fast-changing workplace, which is very heartening.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some, of course, aspire for a University degree.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also heard from employers who agreed with the value of upgrading, but were quite wary about hiring and training someone, only to have them leave in a few years for further studies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope we can find meaningful convergence between the students' aspirations and the employers' needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ultimately, continued training and deepening of relevant skills must translate to better employment and salary outcomes for our Polytechnic and ITE students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue these conversations over the next few months.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Allow me to share an overview of the ideas that have emerged so far, which I see as key priorities for us to address through this review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we recognise our students' diverse interests and aspirations and support them in exploring different options.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes strengthening porosity and flexibility in our education pathways and ensuring strong Education and Career Guidance, or ECG.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Ms Janet Ang that we must help our students be, and I quote her, "always ready to learn", engaged in their studies and inspired about their future careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will look into how to do this better through our review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, our courses and curriculum must remain industry-relevant and prepare students well to enter the workforce after graduation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we have to balance near-term job readiness with career resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want our students to be versatile and able to seize emerging opportunities over the course of their careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we must and we need to invest in life skills, including essential competencies such as cross-cultural communication, critical thinking and collaboration, which are relevant across jobs and disciplines, as well as life outside their workplace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to prepare our students well for life and work, regardless of the pathways they choose after graduation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Fourth, as part of our on-going efforts to help every student achieve their potential and find success, we will build on our experience with UPLIFT in our schools and leverage community partnerships to strengthen support for students with higher needs and enable more of them to achieve their full educational potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Eric Chua spoke passionately about how we should support our ITE students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I wholeheartedly agree and this is, indeed, a key priority.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2019, we announced that, by 2030, we would provide more opportunities for ITE graduates to upgrade beyond a Nitec qualification over the course of their careers, taking into account diverse student aspirations and learning needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to progressively increase Higher Nitec places.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will cater more Polytechnic places for working adults and grow the ITE's Work Study Diploma (WSDip) pathway.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also work closely towards expanding ITE's diploma programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE's Work Study Diplomas or WSDips, and Technical Diplomas have a distinct applied focus and cater to students who benefit from a more hands-on learning style.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will strengthen opportunities for ITE graduates to upgrade to a diploma in the course of their careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: About two-thirds of the ITE graduates in full-time permanent employment reported that their job was related to their course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Having said that, we can always do better to ensure better salary outcomes for our ITE and Polytechnic graduates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE is committed to preparing its students well for the working world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Dr Wan Rizal on the importance of providing meaningful and relevant internship experience for our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I recently met Siti Raudah, who graduated from the Nitec in Logistics Services in 2019.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During her course, Siti interned at YCH Group, a home-grown supply chain solutions company, where she coordinated the movement of freight containers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She made a strong impression and was offered a permanent position after graduation – a very, very positive experience in her internship.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, she is a Logistics Specialist at YCH.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the pace of economic change grows, our graduates will require deeper skills to stay competitive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our companies will also need a more highly skilled workforce to transform.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They complement theory with critical on-the-job training and this is especially evident in the WSDip pathway.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I recently met Alex, who is currently working at air services company dnata and, concurrently, a trainee of our WSDip in Airport Operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While at dnata, Alex picked up specialised skills, such as cool chain handling.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He now leads an Equipment Operator team to ensure the safe and timely movement of inbound and outbound cargo.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is scope to do more for ITE students like Siti and Alex, many of whom benefit from a more hands-on pedagogy which suits their learning pace and style.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will equip our ITE graduates with deeper industry-relevant skills, which provide a stronger foundation for future skills upgrading.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also ensure sufficient flexibility for students of different profiles under this new system to cater to different learning needs and paces.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With this change, we hope to better meet students' aspirations for upgrading, while continuing to meet evolving industry needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will share more details in the months ahead.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One point we heard in our engagements was the importance of course matching.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When students are matched to a course that they are passionate about, they are more motivated to do well and succeed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In recent years, we have taken steps to support students' progress from Secondary school to Polytechnics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have enhanced the Education Career Guidance (ECG) in Secondary schools to help students explore different career pathways and education options.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2019, we expanded the Polytechnic Foundation Programme, or PFP, which prepares selected Polytechnic-bound Normal (Academic) students to enter Polytechnics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the lead up to the implementation of Full Subject-Based Banding in 2024, we are looking at how the PFP can cater to a more diverse profile of Secondary school students, with different strengths and pace of learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We build on this when students enter Polytechnic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, one key effort is the introduction of the Common Entry Programmes or CEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2019, we expanded CEPs to the Business and Information & Digital Technologies clusters, complementing the existing Engineering CEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: CEPs target students interested in a cluster but are undecided about their specific course that they want to undertake.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One student who has benefited is Leonard, who applied for Temasek Polytechnic's or TP's Aerospace Engineering course in 2019 but did not meet the cut-off point.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, Leonard entered TP's Engineering CEP instead, where he was given a feel of TP's other Engineering courses through modules like electrical circuit analysis, digital electronics and programming.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Leonard and his classmates also benefited from talks and hands-on activities conducted by lecturers, ECG counsellors and industry professionals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The CEP helped Leonard affirm his interest in Aerospace Engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Leonard worked hard and has since secured a place in the Aerospace Engineering course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Republic Polytechnic introduced a CEP for the science cluster, and Singapore Polytechnic rolled out their single Media, Arts and Design Course, which functions like a CEP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):    Education must remain an uplifting force for the less advantaged in our society, and help all students achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through UPLIFT, we will continue to collaborate with the community to complement our efforts in schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also strengthen our collaboration with Self-Help groups, including MENDAKI, and explore synergies with other related initiatives such as ComLink and M3.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heading the review at the ITE and polytechnic levels to help our students stay relevant and achieve success amidst an ever-changing world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want all ITE students to aspire to attain their Higher Nitec qualification when they enrol in ITE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This means that we recognise their potential and have confidence in their abilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the first year of their studies, we will expand CEPs to better support polytechnic-bound students in their course selection process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also studying how we might expand the PFP to cater to more students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the Budget debate, Ms Mariam Jaafar spoke about the representation of the Malay community in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics).

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE is committed to support all students, regardless of race, and we will continue to encourage all students, including Malay students, to develop their interests in STEM.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: STEM courses are popular among Malay students as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is just the start of an exciting journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope we can come together to make these ideas a reality.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about MOE’s efforts to foster students’ interest in and appreciation of the Malay Language, and their Mother Tongue Languages (MTLs) in general.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Chairman, let me start by elaborating on MOE’s efforts to promote the use of the Malay Language.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our education system is based on the bilingual policy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A strong foundation in our mother tongue language will enable us to deal with this region more effectively while continuing to stay rooted to our heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is important because we know that the number of children who use Malay as the main language at home is decreasing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past few months, I found out from our Malay Language educators about how we are making adjustments in terms of how and what we teach, to ensure that the Malay Language continues to thrive for a new generation of learners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, Lead Teacher Cikgu Zainaba Omar from Clementi Primary School sets real-world tasks for her students like preparing menus for breakfast and lunch when teaching classifiers like "a pinch of salt" and "a cup of cereal".

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This "task-based approach" helps make language learning more authentic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I was told that her students have become more confident, not just in using the Malay Language, but in the preparation of their own daily meals as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Parents and the community also play a critical role in reinforcing students’ use of the Malay Language beyond the classroom.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE is committed to support their efforts through the Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee (MLLPC).

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of MLLPC’s signature programmes is the Perkasa Warisan camp, conducted in collaboration with the People’s Association and the Malay Activity Executive Council (MESRA).

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The camp provides primary school students an opportunity to deepen their knowledge of Malay culture and heritage through hands-on activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In recent years, we have expanded our efforts to post-secondary students as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the Malay proverb goes, "If we do not split the trunk of the palm tree, how can we get the sago." I applaud these efforts, and am confident that we will continue to find good ways to help the Malay Language thrive as a living language in our homes, schools and community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Bilingualism is a cornerstone of our education system and a good grasp of our Mother Tongue Language, or MTL, can unlock opportunities for our students in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MTLs also help us to remain connected to our heritage and our Singaporean identity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, let me conclude by saying that we have come a long way but our education system cannot remain static.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must respond to changing circumstances as we prepare our children to function confidently in the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And our children must be at the centre of our education system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must work together to ensure that education remains an uplifting force for all and secure a brighter future for Singaporeans and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I thank Members like Mr Patrick Tay, Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Shawn Huang, Ms Carrie Tan and Ms Janet Ang for their thoughtful and timely questions on MOE's support for students' well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The CCE curriculum has an updated, stronger emphasis on mental health and cyber wellness education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Students will learn about topics like differentiating signs of stress and distress, and healthy habits for positive well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise the nexus between increasing digital usage and mental health concerns, even more so amongst our young, who may not know how to regulate their use of social media.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Teachers will work alongside student peer supporters to look out for other students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also work with parents to help guide their young in the use of online media.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During CCE lessons, students will learn to identify risks in the digital space, such as doxing or scams; discern unverified or inappropriate content; and take steps to protect themselves and others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Schools will also guide students to report cyber bullying and harmful content to the online service provider.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In Secondary schools and pre-Universities, students will discuss contemporary issues of interest, such as environmental sustainability, race and religion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through CCE 2021, we hope that students will be equipped to become more resilient, stay mentally healthy and engage one another respectfully and constructively on issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Centre will bring together local and international experts in CCE research and professional development and provide critical thought leadership in this field.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This could establish NIE as a leader for CCE in the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Centre signals our strong commitment to be evidence-based in our curricular and pedagogical approaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of strengthening teachers' professional development for CCE, our courses equip teachers with the skills to teach CCE.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE has regular dialogues with our educators to understand their teaching needs and also be attuned to the issues that students are concerned about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Every Secondary school also has trained specialised CCE teachers to role model and coach other teachers in facilitating challenging CCE discussions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond CCE, our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) are enhancing mental health support by strengthening programmes on mental wellness literacy and awareness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our Polytechnics and ITE have worked with the Health Promotion Board to launch a new mental wellness curriculum for all Year 1 students from 2020 and 2021 respectively to raise awareness and understanding of mental health and also to foster early help-seeking behaviour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The autonomous Universities (AUs) are also promoting mental wellness through briefings during freshmen orientation and University-wide programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From this year, schools will also appoint dedicated Key Personnel to oversee peer support and student well-being matters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They will tap on student peer supporters to help students involved in incidents that affect their well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Alongside peer support, I agree with Mr Darryl David that counselling and guidance must be made readily available to those who need it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Counsellors are vital members of the student support team.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE will continue to grow the number of teacher counsellors and equip them further over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE's efforts complement larger nationwide movements to destigmatise mental health and encourage help-seeking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over 1,500 enthusiastic individuals came together to strengthen the youth mental well-being space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am proud to share that the network has initiated ideas for over 30 potential ground-up projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One team I have met is equipping parents to strengthen emotional literacy in their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another team is working on reframing perceptions of counselling and destigmatising help-seeking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I sincerely thank the network members for their efforts and we warmly welcome others to join them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we emerge from COVID-19 and face on-going challenges, it is going to be a bumpy ride.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But the journey within each and every one of us is not a journey we need to walk alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Let this be our gentle encouragement and steadfast commitment to one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairman, I would now like to reaffirm MOE’s commitment to an important group – students with Special Educational Needs (SEN).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In recent years, we have developed the landscape significantly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mdm Rahayu Mahzam has suggested, we need to grow our students with Special Educational Needs as well as typically developing students in the soft skills that will last them into adult life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Learned Members, such as Ms Denise Phua and Mr Shawn Huang have shared how transitioning between stages can be daunting for students, especially those with SENs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, for pre-school children, moving to P1 can be a major transition, as Mr Patrick Tay had mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To help them along, MOE’s Nurturing Early Learners framework, which is used by MOE Kindergartens (MKs) and other pre-schools, focuses on nurturing children’s curiosity, socio-emotional and motor skills and love for learning, alongside basic literacy and numeracy goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But we recognise that some students with SEN need further support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These students will receive support from Allied Educators (Learning and Behavioural Support) and teachers to develop foundational self-management skills, in small groups and in their classrooms during their P1 year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By the end of P1, students should be able to learn independently in class, with occasional help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One of the first pilot schools is Elias Park Primary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One student, let us call him M, had a difficult time adjusting when he entered P1.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He would lie on the floor and shout in class.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through TRANSIT, our teachers and Allied Educators (LBS) taught M self-management skills, such as working within his personal space and communication.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He was prompted to apply these skills throughout the school day and his parents reinforced them at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, M has a positive learning attitude and he interacts well with his peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For adolescents, entering Secondary school is another milestone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through school-based interventions, such as "Circle of Friends" and peer support structures in every school, schools are building an inclusive culture where peers actively look out for one another and those with Special Educational Needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Denise Phua and Mdm Rahayu Mahzam have asked about MOE's plans to support the students with Special Educational Needs in mainstream schools to better prepare them for the next phase of their lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have increased the number of Allied Educators (LBS) in our schools who work alongside teachers and ECG counsellors to prepare students with Special Educational Needs further studies and work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Mdm Rahayu on the importance of promoting interaction between students with and without SEN.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Mark Chay has pointed out the benefits of parasports.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One key way to sustain relationships between mainstream and SPED schools is through Satellite Partnerships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE will strengthen these partnerships and work with Ms Denise Phua and other sector leaders to increase opportunities for meaningful interaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to work with schools and partners to develop more inclusion opportunities, including parasports that meet our diverse students' needs, develop their strengths and forge mutual understanding and respect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As students progress to IHLs, they can receive course guidance, access arrangements, SEN-related funding for Assistive Technology devices and support services, and also internship support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SPED graduates can take up certifications, like ITE Skills Certificate or Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) or participate in the School-to-Work (S2W) Transition Programme by MOE, MSF and SG Enable, which provides customised training pathways, job matching and work options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I salute the SPED schools for their personalised approach to finding job opportunities and matching their students to jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE affirms its strong commitment to the SPED sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
