text: As Ms Denise Phua has observed, we build schools, provide significant funding and send personnel to work with social service agencies and also to contribute their expertise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I would now like to share about the expansion of capacity of SPED schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will be expanding Grace Orchard School (GOS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is to help meet the demand for places in the west region and enhance the accessibility of SPED schools serving students with Mild Intellectual Disability (MID).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In our work to expand GOS, as with the other seven new SPED schools, we work in consultation with the social service agencies' staff to improve students’ educational experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our students can look forward to (a) new vocational training facilities; (b) larger classrooms and modulation spaces to cater to students who also have ASD; and (c) facilities for PE and sports, like sheltered playgrounds and outdoor fitness areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Alongside enhanced infrastructure, we will develop the skills of all school personnel in both mainstream and SPED schools through coaching, pre-service training and in-service courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our teachers frequently come together across schools, sharing and innovating with their practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We seek to build on the strong spirit of collaboration which we are seeing amongst the SPED schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Thus, we agree wholeheartedly with Ms Denise Phua's call that MOE, together with other agencies, stakeholders and SPED staff, should work together to envision a brighter future for our SPED graduates and their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we strive to make our education system more inclusive where each and every child is recognised, appreciated and supported for who they are, I call on everyone to play a part in making this reality possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We firmly believe that these little steps all add up to build a more inclusive learning environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, as a small country with no natural resources, Singapore’s most valuable assets are our people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Hence, developing our people is a national priority, starting from early childhood, to tertiary education for our youths, and continuing education and training (CET) for adults to support their careers and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Lifelong learning empowers each Singaporean to chart his or her own journey in life and gain fulfilment at work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The SkillsFuture movement was started in 2014 to take lifelong learning to the next level.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It creates multiple pathways for our people to upskill and reskill, either to develop mastery in their skills, or pick up new skills to start a new career path.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SkillsFuture supports Singaporeans to learn for life, for lifelong employability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One of the points highlighted in the Emerging Stronger Conversations is that lifelong learning is necessary to keep our workforce resilient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have built a comprehensive eco-system of training support and skills pathways over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When COVID-19 struck, we were able to tap on the eco-system to support our graduating students and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have taken great care to support fresh graduates from ITE, Polytechnics and Universities as they make the transition into working life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: And in my MOM speech just now, I spoke about the SGUnited Traineeships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) have stepped up career facilitation assistance to the graduates, and provided free CET modules to help boost their employability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Many of our graduates have taken courses in areas, such as data analytics and finance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Mr Darryl David on the benefits of Work-Study Programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes bridge fresh graduates’ transition into the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Such opportunities are available at the diploma, post-diploma and degree levels, providing an applied learning pathway for our graduates to continue developing their skillsets in their chosen industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To ensure continued availability of such opportunities during this period, we have introduced wage support to employers that are participating in Place-and-Train Work-Study programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har highlighted the need to evolve our reskilling pathways to address job opportunities in the care, digital and green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This has been a key focus in our efforts to support mid-career Singaporeans whose livelihoods have been affected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We engaged key partners to provide training through the SGUnited Skills programmes and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways, a company training programme, to help jobseekers move into new jobs, particularly in the growth areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For the healthcare sector, one such training partner is the HMI Institute of Health Sciences (HMI Institute).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As part of the SGUnited Skills Programme, HMI Institute provides employment facilitation and career advisory services to its trainees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Since August 2020, HMI Institute has enrolled 360 individuals, many of whom are mid-careerists, contributing towards the much needed pipeline of manpower for our healthcare-related roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will provide continued support for Singaporeans to learn and thrive, as our jobs and workplaces change, and as businesses transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In the next phase, we will expand the capacity of in-demand courses courses with good hiring opportunities in sectors such as infocomm technology (ICT) and media, professional services, healthcare and advanced manufacturing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will keep the duration of most courses to no more than six months, so that the trainees can transition to employment quickly, with the support of the training partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While the pandemic has created a challenging operating environment, it also presents opportunities for employers to upskill their workers during the downtime, thereby getting them ready for new business processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have supported employers in sending their workers for training through the Enhanced Training Support Package (ETSP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The ETSP supports eight sectors that have been more severely affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: About 155,000 training places have been taken up in these sectors, benefiting more than 72,000 employees across 1,300 companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: ETSP has been particularly well-utilised by the tourism and aviation sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will extend the ETSP to 31 December 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will allow the firms to send more workers for industry-relevant training to help their workforce emerge stronger post-COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Due to the pandemic, a much larger proportion of training last year was delivered in a blended or online modality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Indeed, online training can provide greater convenience and reach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) is working with training providers to assess how this can continue to be enhanced while ensuring that the learning outcomes are met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar noted that while COVID-19 has limited opportunities for overseas exposure, leading global companies could be tapped to provide this in virtual formats for Singaporean workers and students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We agree and have been finding ways to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Some of our IHL students have been able to take on internships with overseas start-ups under the Global Innovation Alliance (Innovators Academy) programme via "remote internships".

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to explore how we can engage our partner companies and Queen Bees to expand such opportunities to more individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Even as we tackle the near-term challenges that the pandemic has brought about, it is important that we continue to keep an eye on the future that lies beyond.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are therefore pressing on with our plans for the Next Bound of SkillsFuture, which Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: A key thrust of the Next Bound of SkillsFuture is enhancing the role of enterprises in developing their workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har has emphasised the importance of this and I fully agree.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Queen Bee companies include private sector leading firms, such as IBM and Prudential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They form business communities with enterprises to address common skills needs and co-create solutions in their sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked how our IHL educators can strengthen support for our SMEs' training efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, our Polytechnic lecturers do industry attachments with companies, including SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have been ramping this up to ensure that they remain in touch with industry developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As they undergo such attachments, they could use their institutional knowledge to help bring technology solutions to enterprises and also help their host companies strengthen their training plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, companies can benefit from consultancy services provided by the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning or NACE, for short.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG's skills frameworks serve as an important common reference point across training providers and employers, as they provide key information on career pathways, job roles, as well as existing and emerging skills required for the job roles in different sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Mr Patrick Tay that we need to encourage the adoption of the Skills Frameworks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: That was why I was happy when the Institution of Engineers, Singapore (IES) established a National Engineering Career Progression Pathway, in alignment with the Skills FFramework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The scheme opens a non-academic route for engineering technicians and technologists to move towards the Chartered Engineer status, hence promoting employee recognition and career development based on technical skills and work experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: IES has set a strong example of how industry associations can take the lead in building new skills-based pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I hope to see more associations drive such change in their respective domains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Complementing the focus on enterprises is our effort to encourage individuals to take ownership of their skills development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked for the latest statistics concerning SkillsFuture Credit usage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The number of claims also increased by about 30% from 2019 to 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to provide personalised guidance, in the form of SkillsFuture Advice workshops and seminars and Skills and Training Advisory at job fairs and community events, many of which are actually organised by the CDCs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For this group, besides the common course offerings, they can also choose from 30 SkillsFuture courses customised for them, covering areas such as ICT, food and beverage and customer service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue looking at how to strengthen the training eco-system to support their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Under the Next Bound of SkillsFuture, we will also focus on helping mid-career workers transition to new and emerging employment opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To this end, we have been ramping up our provision of training programmes and strengthening the partnership between SSG and WSG to improve employment outcomes of Train-and-Place programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: From July to December 2020, we launched over 300 programmes, including SGUnited Skills and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training programmes which I mentioned earlier on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Looking beyond the pandemic, we expect to build on the groundwork and evolve these programmes into Career Transition Programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will strengthen our slate of offerings to our mid-career workers in their steady state.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We constantly seek to ensure that our training programmes deliver outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our course fee subsidies are tiered, with the highest tier tied to those with work-related outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Given the tight fiscal environment, we are also mindful about how we resource the Next Bound of SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, we are continually reviewing existing schemes, to focus our funding on training that delivers strong employment outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Second, when the Enhanced Training Support Package ends this year, we will revise the absentee payroll funding to a more sustainable rate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This complements the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit that will continue beyond 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I am heartened by the tenacity demonstrated by Singaporeans in the past year, from our workers to employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As we set our sights on economic recovery, we will continue to support Singaporeans in their lifelong learning journey towards skills mastery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through SkillsFuture, we will enable Singaporeans to strive for their goals, and emerge stronger together.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Chairman, I have two questions for MOE for the Minister first.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And that there will be few sacred cows – or stones! – that he will be not willing to turn and look at.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And what about stones like PSLE which we have discussed much in the past?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And how to turn, for example, to build on strengths of some of the tuition centres so that parents, families and students do not have to rely so much on tuition centres.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The second one is for the Minister of State Sun Xueling.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Chairman, our starting point is that we have a good education system today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not a system that is broken and in need of a complete overhaul.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But at the same time, we keep an open mind.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are not satisfied with the status quo.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We keep on improving and we continue to do so by experimenting, trying out new approaches, understanding what works, what does not work so well and then, step by step making careful systematic effective implementation to improve the system continuously.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Year-by-year, you may not see a lot of change but, in fact, it all adds up when you take a step back.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Just think about some of the things that have been happening over the recent years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The emphasis on 21 CCs and CCEs in schools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The change to aptitude-based admissions to Universities; is a very important step.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The removal of streaming and the move to full subject-based banding.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are not done in an ad hoc fashion.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They are all part of a coherent reform to make our system better, to encourage students to pursue their strengths and interests, to instil the joy of learning in every child.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the direction of where we are heading.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you talk about a roadmap, what are we trying to achieve, basically, we want to continue this effort to instil in every child competencies and skills that will prepare them better for the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to continue to build diverse and flexible pathway so that we can nurture diverse talent, so that people with differing abilities and strengths can pursue those passions and interests and excel across a whole range of different areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we want to uplift every child, providing much more support to the disadvantaged and vulnerable groups, including children with special needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those are our priorities and we will continue to lift every stone, look at every issue, potentially slay a few more sacred cows in order to ensure that we have an excellent education system to bring out the best in every child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MOE's overarching goal is to provide quality education for all students with special needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But this must be balanced with ensuring that they develop educationally in a setting that best fits their needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And where there are more specific needs that these children with special needs have, they are then supported in the SPED schools.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Earlier, I have talked about expanding the range of SPED schools that are available to best fit and best serve the students that we have who have special needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the second point that Ms Denise Phua had about lifelong learning, we share her views and her aspirations and belief that our students with special needs should lead meaningful lives and they should continually upgrade their skills and be active in the community and also contribute to society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With regards to supporting SPED graduates in lifelong learning, both myself as well as my colleague Minister of State Gan have talked about the variety of training supports available to our students with special needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This includes broad-based training support such as course fee subsidies and SkillsFuture Credit for those aged 25 and above, and also just like my colleague Minister of State Gan has spoken about, SkillsFuture Singapore has also worked with SG Enable to roll out more than 30 SkillsFuture Credit-eligible courses that are customised for our fellow friends, residents with special needs, students, and they cover areas such as information and communications technology (ICT), F&B and customer service.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are fully aligned with the thinking that Ms Denise Phua has, that there should be continuous lifelong learning opportunities for our students with special needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But that said, I think we both can agree even the best and most hardworking teacher would generally be unable to assist their children as much as they would wish if they are hamstrung by heavy loads.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: When I call for smaller class sizes, I am implicitly calling for MOE to provide our teachers with the environment such that their quality may be fully experienced by the children because they are not stretched too thinly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: If what we are concerned about is an ability to maximise the impact of this existing high quality teachers, if we are not going to have an outright reduction in class sizes, perhaps we will consider supplying teaching aides or assistants to the classrooms teaching the tuition-intensive subjects that I mentioned, namely mathematics and the languages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Assoc Prof Lim for acknowledging the hard work and efforts of our educators in schools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think we are on the same page.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Number one, as I said, MOE will continue to ensure that we have a high quality teaching force and make sure that we have healthy pupil-teacher ratios.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Already, our ratios today are comparable with OECD standards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is not for a lack of teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, we will do everything we can to support our teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Assoc Prof Lim highlighted that because of the heavy loads of the teachers, they may be hamstrung and may not be able to be as effective as they would like.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to review with all our educators what is the best way to allocate their time across the different areas of work that they do, both in classrooms and outside of classrooms, bearing in mind that when you make these OECD comparisons, many other countries do not have the same kind of CCA provisions that we have in Singapore, neither do they have teachers spending time in these areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have asked our educators before, "Would you like to cut back your time on CCAs?" Many of them said no.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They value their time in CCAs because they recognise that this time outside of the classroom is important for holistic development of students.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue this conversation and engagement with our teachers to give them our full support from the MOE headquarters and whatever they need to get their job done and, as I said, to provide holistic teaching and learning for every child.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to compliment and congratulate MOE and ITE management for improving the quality of ITE tremendously over the past decade.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Like Mr Eric Chua, I have met many excellent ITE youths who help out at my constituency's events.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Like what Minister Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman has said, many of these youths lack family support and guidance when they were much younger and therefore, they draw inspiration from their ITE teachers.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Besides teaching, all these class advisors do general management, they facilitate social and financial assistance and they also perform the role of counsellor.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Moreover, ITE is also admitting more and more students with special needs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Chairman, first, let me thank Mr Don Wee for his recognition of the effort of ITE teachers in educating our students in ITE.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Indeed, ITE is more than just an educational institution.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They acknowledge that they have a strong social role in supporting their students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: ITE absorbs and takes in students from diverse backgrounds and with diverse abilities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As Mr Don Wee mentioned, the teachers have done a tremendous amount of work in not only just providing training in terms of the skills required by the students to get better outcomes in terms of their work, but they also provide a lot of support emotionally.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I have met many of the students, even those who have graduated.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They tell me that the one thing that always makes them remember their ITE education is indeed their teachers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Sometimes, after they have graduated, after they finish their National Service, they come back and they want to speak to their teachers to get some career guidance.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, thank you so much, Mr Don Wee, for acknowledging the work of our ITE teachers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Yes, we will continue to look at how best we can support our teachers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These are officers that are specifically recruited to help students with special needs, the varying needs of these students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will continue to monitor the learning needs of our ITE students and we are prepared to enhance the support if necessary, including for our SEN students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For those students who do come from other disadvantaged backgrounds, we also support ITE with social emotional counsellors to help them with some of their challenges.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Many of the students come with very challenging backgrounds.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the same time, sometimes, they get engaged in part-time employment because of the financial circumstances they are in.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We provide financial support for them and we will continue to help them, because we want them to aspire to have higher qualifications.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As I mentioned earlier, with the curricular structure review, we want all ITE students to aspire to attain their Higher Nitec qualification when they enter ITE.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: One last point I want to add is that, in recognition of our ITE's staff, we introduced the ITE Staff Appreciation Day last year for the first time.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Last year, it was on 6 November 2020.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And we will recognise the first Friday of November each year as the Polytechnic-ITE Staff Appreciation Day, akin to Teachers' Day, but specifically for our teachers in the IHLs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But could I ask specifically whether as part of the review, we can look into removing the quotas and the punitive implications of the lower grades?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I also thank the Minister for changing "sacred cows" into "sacred stones".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: That is much better because we do not need to slay the cows anymore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, if you look at the literature or if you look at education systems around the world, the quality of teachers, as I said before, matters a lot in outcomes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are fortunate in Singapore to have capable, motivated, high quality teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I said just now, we have been in discussion with the our teachers' unions on this matter.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to engage them and work with them, taking in their feedback and suggestions to see how the system can be further improved.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Patrick Tay, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I would also like to thank our educators, tripartite partners as well as stakeholders in the education eco-system because it is going to get tougher and we really need to stay ahead of the times and of course, ahead of the curve, particularly, with this next normal and a lot of disruptions, digitalisation and the drive towards continuing education and training.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
